title: Kynex by QI Spine: Launch plan
subtitle: Weekly plan from kickoff to go-live at every QI Spine centre

tasks.name: Present plan, project charter & roles to management
tasks.detail: Approval names the Project Head as the single point of contact, with final say on scope, priorities and releases.

tasks.name: Kickoff: team starts
tasks.detail: Tue 1 Dec 2026

tasks.name: Week 1 discovery workshops
tasks.detail: Cover CRM, payment, video, cloud, the centre list, languages, patient data, helpdesk, reporting rhythm and the tracker app decision.

tasks.name: Team size & track set-up
tasks.detail: The Project Head decides how many developers go on each build track. That number sets the build speed.

tasks.name: Team onboarding & codebase walkthrough
tasks.detail: Each team member gets their role, the working rules and a walkthrough of the Kynex codebase.

tasks.name: Module planning & reviews (every 3 weeks)
tasks.detail: The Project Head sets each module's scope and accepts or rejects it at the module review.

tasks.name: Friday status update to management
tasks.detail: One page every Friday covering progress against the Gantt, risks and decisions needed.

tasks.name: Plan, charter & budget approved
tasks.detail: Management signs off the plan, the Project Head charter and the cost list.

tasks.name: Demo 1: foundations + design direction
tasks.detail: Shows Module 1 and the signed-off wireframes and design system.

tasks.name: Demo 2: patient app, doctor dashboard, bookings & payments
tasks.detail: End of Modules 2 and 3.

tasks.name: Demo 3: consults, chat, outcome scores, pain report
tasks.detail: End of Modules 4 and 5.

tasks.name: Demo 4: full app + feature freeze
tasks.detail: End of Modules 6 and 7. No new features after this date.

tasks.name: Go / no-go decision
tasks.detail: The Project Head and management decide, using the dry-run results.

tasks.name: Launch report + Phase 2 roadmap
tasks.detail: Covers results against the success targets and the next phase.

tasks.name: Phase 1 · User research: patients of all ages, physios, front desk
tasks.detail: Includes patients aged 60+ and people who are not comfortable with phones.

tasks.name: Phase 1 · Personas, user flows & wireframes for all 7 modules
tasks.detail: The structure is settled before developers build. The Project Head approves it.

tasks.name: Phase 1 · Design system: 'Kynex by QI Spine'
tasks.detail: Colours, type, components, large-text and accessibility rules.

tasks.name: Wireframes & design system signed off
tasks.detail: Signed off by the Project Head.

tasks.name: Phase 2 · Screen design, one module ahead of development
tasks.detail: Final screens for each module are ready before that module starts.

tasks.name: Phase 2 · Usability test at the end of every module
tasks.detail: Includes 60+ and low-tech users. Success means they finish key tasks without help.

tasks.name: Phase 3 · Visual polish: motion, micro-interactions, empty and error states
tasks.detail: A longer, dedicated polish phase near the end. This is where the app becomes 'premium'.

tasks.name: Phase 3 · Accessibility audit & large-text pass
Phase 3 · Final usability round at the dry-run centres
Camera engine & AI: 100+ exercises, low-end Android speed
tasks.detail: The Project Head builds and owns this.

tasks.name: M1 · Foundations: cloud, sign-in, roles, consent, audit log, pipeline
tasks.detail: All developers. Week 3 of every module is for testing and polish. See the Build modules tab.

tasks.name: Track A · M2 · Patient app & core rehab loop
tasks.detail: Includes the New Year week (lighter).

tasks.name: Track B · M3 · Doctor dashboard, plans, bookings & payments
Track A · M4 · Care & communication: video consults, chat, reminders
Track B · M5 · Clinical insights: outcome scores, 3D pain report, education
Track A · M6 · Languages, AI voice coach, Android & iPhone apps
Track B · M7 · Admin & analytics, CRM sync
Feature freeze
Hardening: bug fixes, speed, security fixes, accessibility
Release candidate
tasks.detail: Accepted by the Project Head.

tasks.name: CRM: access, field mapping, data contract
tasks.detail: Company IT gives access. The Project Head approves the mapping. The build is in M7.

tasks.name: Payment gateway account (needed for M3)
tasks.detail: Opened in the company's name.

tasks.name: WhatsApp Business & SMS accounts (needed for M4)
tasks.detail: WhatsApp verification can take several weeks.

tasks.name: Video consult service account (needed for M4)
Patient data import (if week 1 decides yes)
QI Spine exercise database handover (100+ exercises)
tasks.detail: Everything downstream depends on this.

tasks.name: Exercise list received
Exercise rules & rep-count criteria, per exercise
tasks.detail: Written with the Project Head, who encodes them in the camera engine.

tasks.name: Outcome questionnaires chosen (pain, function)
tasks.detail: Needed for M5.

tasks.name: AI video pilot: 10 exercises, physio review

tasks.name: Video route decided: AI, or physio shoot

Module testing (week 3 of every module)
Full regression

Training material & how-to videos

Holi / Good Friday week: buffer only, no changes
GO-LIVE: all QI Spine centres
Hypercare: fast fixes, daily report to management
tasks.detail: 4 weeks after go-live.

tasks.name: Phase 2 planning

components.name: Cloud & environments
components.what: India-region hosting on the company cloud. Development, test and live environments. Daily backups, monitoring and alerts.
components.done: The app runs on the company cloud, and a backup restore has been tested.

components.name: Release pipeline
components.what: Automatic tests and build on every change. Releases need the Project Head's approval.
components.done: No release can go out without passing tests and the Project Head's sign-off.

components.name: Sign-in & accounts
components.what: Patients sign in with their mobile number and a one-time code. Staff sign in with email and a second step. Roles: patient, physio/doctor, centre admin, management. Lockout and session timeout.
components.done: Every role sees only what it should. Tested on low-end phones.

components.name: Consent & privacy
components.what: Consent screens, the privacy notice, and requests to download or delete data. Wording comes from Company Legal.
components.done: Legal has approved the wording, and consent is recorded per patient.

components.name: Audit log
components.what: A record of who did what, and when, for every clinical change.
components.done: Every plan change and review shows who made it and when.

components.name: Design system in code
components.what: Shared buttons, cards, forms and charts from the UX design system, with large-text and accessibility settings.
components.done: Every screen uses the shared parts, and large text never breaks a layout.

components.name: Onboarding
components.what: Welcome screens, language choice, a phone placement check, camera permission and a first-session tutorial.
components.done: A first-time user aged 60+ reaches their first exercise without help.

components.name: Today screen
components.what: Today's exercises, start or continue the session, streak, next visit and the care team.
components.done: One tap from opening the app to starting the session.

components.name: Guided session
components.what: Pain check-in and red-flag questions, camera counting with voice, tap-to-count fallback, rest timers, 'how did it feel', and pain after.
components.done: A full session finishes without help, and a red flag stops it and alerts the clinic.

components.name: Camera engine (Project Head)
components.what: Rep counting, holds and form tips for 100+ exercises. Runs on the phone, so no video is uploaded.
components.done: Counts match a physio's count in lab tests, and it runs smoothly on a low-end Android phone.

components.name: Exercise player
components.what: Instructor video, steps, precautions and where to place the phone.
components.done: Every exercise has a video, or a clear placeholder.

components.name: Reports & progress
components.what: Session report, replay of a rep, and progress over the weeks.
components.done: The patient can see their progress over the past weeks.

components.name: Patient list & attention flags
components.what: Patients sorted by urgency: red flags, rising pain, missed sessions, form problems, reports to review.
components.done: A doctor finds who needs attention in under 10 seconds.

components.name: Plan builder
components.what: Exercise library search, dose, days, notes, and templates per condition.
components.done: A doctor prescribes a plan in under 2 minutes.

components.name: Session review
components.what: Movement replay, rep timeline, notes, and 'mark as reviewed'.
components.done: The doctor's note reaches the patient straight away.

components.name: Bookings & calendar
components.what: Centre and video slots, doctor hours and leave, waiting list, booking reminders.
components.done: A patient books, moves or cancels a visit without calling the centre.

components.name: Payments
components.what: Pay for visits and packages through the payment gateway, with receipts. Refunds are done by an admin.
components.done: Test payments, receipts and refunds work end to end.

components.name: Video consults
components.what: Join from the app or dashboard through a ready-made video service, with a waiting room and notes after the call.
components.done: A 15-minute call holds up on a 4G connection.

components.name: Care-team chat
components.what: Patient-to-physio messages and photos, quick replies, office hours, and escalation to the doctor.
components.done: Messages arrive within seconds, and office hours are shown clearly.

components.name: Reminders
components.what: Push notifications plus WhatsApp and SMS for sessions, visits and missed sessions.
components.done: Reminders reach patients in their own language and at the right time.

components.name: Symptoms & red-flag alerts
components.what: The patient reports a symptom and the clinic is alerted, with a log of the follow-up.
components.done: Every red flag reaches the clinic within a minute.

components.name: Outcome scores
components.what: Standard pain and function questionnaires, scheduled automatically, with scores shown over time.
components.done: The doctor sees the score trend on the patient page.

components.name: 3D pain map & body report
components.what: The patient marks pain areas on a 3D body. The report is shared with the doctor.
components.done: Pain areas are saved and shown over time.

components.name: Education library
components.what: Articles and short videos for each condition, assigned along with the plan.
components.done: Content is assigned automatically by condition.

components.name: Adherence & recovery trends
components.what: Charts of sessions done, range of movement and pain over time, for the doctor.
components.done: Every chart also has a table view.

modules.name: Languages, AI voice coach & mobile apps

components.name: Translation system
components.what: All app text in English, Hindi and 10-15 regional languages, with a language switch.
components.done: Every screen is checked in every language, with no cut-off text.

components.name: AI voice coach
components.what: Spoken counts, cues and form tips in every language.
components.done: A native speaker has approved the voice for each language.

components.name: Android & iPhone apps
components.what: The Kynex web app wrapped as store apps, with camera and notification permissions, store listings and screenshots.
components.done: The apps pass Play Store and App Store review.

components.name: Weak-internet sessions
components.what: A session keeps working on a weak connection and syncs later.
components.done: A session done in airplane mode syncs once the phone is back online.

components.name: Management dashboard
components.what: Centres, active patients, adherence, outcomes and revenue, as a live view.
components.done: The numbers match the source data for a test week.

components.name: Centre admin
components.what: Staff accounts, centre settings, and managing the exercise library.
components.done: A centre is set up in under 30 minutes.

components.name: CRM sync
components.what: Patients and appointments flow to and from the CRM.
components.done: No duplicates or lost records over a 2-week test.

components.name: Activity & exports
components.what: An activity feed, the audit view, and exports for management.
components.done: An export opens cleanly in Excel.

components.name: Speed & stability
components.what: App start time, camera frame rate on low-end phones, and crash fixes.
components.done: 99.5% of sessions crash-free in the dry run.

components.name: Security fixes
components.what: Fixes for the issues found in the penetration test.
components.done: No high-severity issues remain open.

components.name: Accessibility
components.what: Fixes from the UX accessibility audit.
components.done: Every key task works with large text and a screen reader.

roles.title: Project Head: product manager & core builder
duties: Only point of contact between the project and management
Owns the vision, roadmap, scope and priorities. Every change request comes through the Project Head.
Decides the team size and how developers are split across the two build tracks
Writes the specs and acceptance criteria for every module
Builds and owns the camera engine, the AI and the architecture
Approves every design, code merge, content item and release
Runs module planning and reviews, the Friday updates and the demos
Has admin access to every company account (cloud, stores, repository, payments)

roles.title: Management (sponsor)
duties: Approves the plan, the budget and the team allocation
Unblocks access to other departments (IT, Legal, centres)
Attends the demos and takes the go/no-go decision with the Project Head

roles.title: UI/UX designer
duties: Phase 1: research, user flows, wireframes and the 'Kynex by QI Spine' design system
Phase 2: final screens, one module ahead of development, and a usability test after each module
Phase 3: visual polish, motion, accessibility and the final usability round
Works from the Project Head's specs and to the Project Head's sign-off

roles.title: Developers (2 build tracks)
duties: Build each 3-week module from the Project Head's specs, in the Kynex codebase
Track A builds the patient app, care and communication, languages and the mobile apps
Track B builds the doctor dashboard, bookings, payments, clinical insights, admin and the CRM
Follow the Project Head's code review and release process

roles.title: Physio team (2-3, 1-2 days a week)
duties: Hand over the QI Spine exercise database (100+ exercises)
Define the rules and form criteria for each exercise
Review the AI instructor videos, or do the physio shoot if it's needed
Choose the outcome measures, write the education content, and review clinical text in each language
Run the clinical acceptance tests

roles.title: QA
duties: Write the test plan and run the low-end Android device lab
Test in week 3 of every module, then run the full regression and the release checks
Monitor the dry run

roles.title: Company IT & Legal
duties: Set up the cloud, store, payment, WhatsApp and video accounts in the company's name, with the Project Head as admin
Provide CRM access and the security test
Legal: DPDP, consent, privacy policy, terms and any medical-device question

roles.title: Centre staff
duties: Take part in the dry run and the training
Onboard patients and give first-line support

risks.risk: Two build tracks need enough developers
risks.mitigation: About 2 developers per track. The Project Head sets the team size in week 1. With fewer developers, modules run one after another and the go-live date is reviewed at Demo 2.
3-week modules with a test week each, feature freeze on 26 Feb, a follow-up release lane, and a weekly scope review by the Project Head

risks.risk: Shared team members get pulled onto other work
risks.mitigation: Management names each person and their % time in week 1, committed until 30 Apr

risks.risk: QI Spine exercise database arrives late
risks.mitigation: Needed by 18 Dec. The Project Head escalates to management if it slips.

risks.risk: AI videos not approved for 100+ exercises
risks.mitigation: A 10-exercise pilot and a decision by 8 Jan. A physio shoot (7-8 days over 5 weeks) is kept as the backup.

risks.risk: Delays opening WhatsApp, payment, video and CRM access
risks.mitigation: Applications go in during week 2, before the modules that need them. Company IT owns them.
Submit by 26 Feb, leaving 3 weeks of buffer. Patients can use the web app link either way.
AI translation plus native-speaker review. Centre-region languages are done first.

risks.risk: Camera speed on low-end Android phones
risks.mitigation: Device lab from week 2. The Project Head owns the engine.

risks.risk: Centre staff slow to adopt the app
risks.mitigation: Dry run, training at every centre, helpdesk and 4 weeks of hypercare
Already built into the plan. Holi week is buffer only.

decisions: Approve this plan and the Project Head charter: single point of contact, with final say on scope, priorities, team size and releases
Name the team members and their % time, committed until 30 Apr 2027. About 4 developers allows two build tracks.
Approve the budget (cost list presented in week 1)
Name the contacts for IT/cloud, CRM and Legal
Confirm the list of centres, which sets the regional languages
Decide who staffs the patient helpdesk and whether current patients are imported
Agree the reporting rhythm and whether to build a project tracker app

targets.target: Every QI Spine centre is live on 31 Mar 2027
90%+ of usability-test users, including those aged 60+, finish key tasks without help
A patient is onboarded in under 3 minutes; a doctor prescribes a plan in under 2 minutes
70% of new rehab patients at live centres are onboarded in the first 4 weeks
60%+ of patients exercise at least 3 times a week
Crash-free sessions at 99.5% or above; app store rating of 4.5 or above
Critical issues are fixed within 24 hours during hypercare

assumptions: The team starts on Tue 1 Dec 2026. Week 0 (this week) is for preparation and the pitch to management.
Every build module takes 3 weeks: week 1 build, week 2 build and connect, week 3 test and polish
Two build tracks run side by side and need about 4 developers. The Project Head decides the team size, and that sets the speed.
Team: 1 UI/UX designer, 2-3 physios at 1-2 days a week and 1 QA, all on board by week 2
UX works in three phases: structure first (research, flows, wireframes), screens one module ahead, then a long polish phase
Exercise videos are AI-generated by preference. A physio shoot of 100+ exercises (7-8 shoot days over 5 weeks) is the backup.
The phone apps wrap the existing Kynex web app; we are not writing separate native apps
Chat, video consults, payments and WhatsApp use ready-made services rather than being built from scratch
Languages: AI translation plus native-speaker review. Centre-region languages are done first.
All accounts are owned by the company, with the Project Head as admin
The success targets are proposals, to be confirmed with management in week 1
